correctness.rationale: The stationary two-sided OU convolution is conditionally Gaussian with dimensionless variance V=2γ∫_0∞e^(−2γs)q^(2N(−s,0])ds, supported on (0,1). The independent Poisson backward age gives U=1−V=A(1−q²V′), A~Beta(r/(2γ),1) independent. For every 0<u<1−q², conditioning gives P(U≤u)=u^α E(1−q²V′)^(−α), hence exact endpoint density αB u^(α−1). The variance generator gives m_n=n m_(n−1)/(n+α(1−q^(2n))), and the generalized binomial series converges since q<1. In the Gaussian-mixture density, a local Laplace change u=z/s yields Γ(α+1)B s^(−α); the region u≥δ has an exponential bound. Coupling the stationary variance functionals proves strict B monotonicity and divergence as q approaches one. Finite verifier run from the package path passed 336 exact and 10 high-precision tests; those tests supplement, not replace, the proof. Fixed q and all positive physical rates are included, with q=1 expressly excluded from the tail theorem.

value.rationale: A direct physically motivated problem in a harmonically confined stochastic-resetting gas is to predict rare large displacements at fixed trap diffusivity and reset parameters. The explicit power correction |x|^(−r/γ) changes rare-event likelihoods despite an unchanged Gaussian exponential rate, and the model-specific coefficient gives an exact discriminant of reset amplitude via extremes. The exact variance-deficit edge probability identifies the mechanism behind this robustness, while divergence as q→1 shows a meaningful nonuniform boundary between non-equilibrium resets and equilibrium Gaussian behavior. This is more than re-labeling a moment identity or an unmotivated finite special case. Limitations: no new finite-time, multidimensional or non-Poisson claim.
